Answer: C
Reason: The axial CT image shows an ill-defined soft tissue mass/infiltrate in the central mediastinum adjacent to the trachea, which correlates with the clinical presentation of dysphonia and is characteristic of a primary tracheal malignancy like squamous cell carcinoma. Peripheral nodules or infiltrates (Options A, B) would not typically cause direct laryngeal/tracheal symptoms, and there is clearly a pathological finding present (ruling out D).
